name: Contract and manage owner-operators
summary: Owner-operators are self-employed drivers who own their tractors and lease them to the carrier under a written contract. The owner-operator coordinator screens applicants, safety qualifies and road-tests the driver, a technician inspects the tractor, and the coordinator writes the lease, plates the unit under the carrier's accounts and hands it to a driver manager; settlements set up pay and deductions. The same team handles renewals, tractor changes and terminations, where escrow refunds and final deductions are often disputed. The work is slow because it waits on the applicant's documents, the shop, the driver trainer and the plate office, and because lease terms, fuel surcharge and chargebacks must match what settlements later pays.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian LTL and truckload carrier of about 3,000 employees with about 380 owner-operators leased to its truckload division.
baseline.notes: Contract actions are new applications, renewals or tractor changes, and terminations.

trigger: An owner-operator applies, a lease comes up for renewal or the tractor changes, or either side gives notice to end a lease.
end_state: A new owner-operator is leased on and dispatched, a lease is renewed or amended, a lease is ended with the final settlement paid, or the application is declined or withdrawn.

volume.seasonality: More applications in spring and late summer before the autumn peak; fewer starts in December. Spot rates were very high in 2021 and early 2022, pulling some owner-operators to run under their own authority.

evidence.note: 380 owner-operators with annual turnover of 30% to 40% (author's estimate, below the 90% ATA figure for company drivers at large US fleets) give 10 to 13 new leases and as many terminations a month; at about 50% of applications signed that is about 25 applications; plus about 14 renewals or tractor changes. The organisation file's 6 to 16 a month appears to count new leases only.

Touch time of about 2 hours per action on 50 actions a month gives about 0.8 FTE; the organisation file's 4 coordinators also answer owner-operators' daily questions and disputes, which are not modelled as cases here.

steps.name: Log the contract action
steps.description: The owner-operator coordinator opens the request, which is a new application from the website or a recruiter, an upcoming lease renewal or unit change, or a termination notice, and logs it in the owner-operator tracking spreadsheet with the unit number and due date.

evidence.note: Mix of actions estimated from 380 owner-operators: about 25 applications, 14 renewals or unit changes and 11 terminations a month.

steps.name: Screen the application
steps.description: The coordinator reads the application and checks years of experience, the tractor's year, make and kilometres, whether the applicant can cross the border (passport, FAST card) and the lanes wanted, and phones the applicant and one previous carrier. Applicants with an old tractor or a poor record are declined at once.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate. Decline share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Qualify the driver and build the driver file
steps.description: The compliance specialist orders the driver's abstract and criminal record check, gets previous-employer references, sends the driver for a pre-contract drug and alcohol test for US work, and builds the driver qualification file in the safety system. The owner-operator's driver must meet the same standard as a company driver.

control.basis: Provincial National Safety Code carrier safety programs and, for US trips, FMCSA driver qualification and drug and alcohol testing rules (49 CFR Parts 391 and 382)

evidence.note: Driver qualification for owner-operators mirrors company drivers under provincial National Safety Code carrier rules and US 49 CFR Part 391 and 382 for cross-border work; texts not opened, so tier C.

steps.name: Road test the driver
steps.description: A driver trainer rides with the driver for a road test covering a pre-trip inspection, coupling, backing and highway driving, and scores it on the company form. A failed test ends the application or sends the driver for more training.

control.basis: Company driver qualification policy: road test before first dispatch

evidence.note: Road tests before hire are common carrier policy; times and pass rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request tractor and business documents
steps.description: The coordinator emails the checklist of documents needed: proof of tractor ownership and registration, the last annual safety inspection, bobtail and physical damage insurance certificates, the GST/HST (and QST in Quebec) number, incorporation papers if incorporated, and a void cheque for direct deposit.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Owner-operator gathers and sends documents
steps.description: The owner-operator collects the papers from the insurer, the bank and the accountant, often between trips, and scans or photographs them back to the coordinator. Missing insurance certificates are the usual hold-up.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check documents and insurance
steps.description: The coordinator compares the registration and ownership with the tractor's VIN, confirms the inspection is current, calls the insurer or broker to confirm the certificates are in force, and checks the business number. Missing or expired papers go back to the owner-operator.

error.defect_description: An insurance certificate that lapses soon, or a wrong VIN, is accepted.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Owner-operator drives the tractor to the company shop
steps.description: The owner-operator books an inspection slot and drives the tractor to the nearest company shop, usually between loads or on a day off, which can mean a few hours of driving.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Inspect the tractor at the company shop
steps.description: A heavy-duty technician carries out the carrier's intake inspection on the company's periodic inspection form: brakes, steering, tires, lights, frame, coupling devices, exhaust and the cab. Defects are listed and the tractor is passed or failed.

control.basis: National Safety Code periodic vehicle inspection standard and company equipment policy: unit inspected before it is leased on

evidence.note: Carrier intake inspection to the periodic inspection standard (National Safety Code Standard 11) is common practice; text not opened. Times and failure rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Owner-operator repairs the defects
steps.description: The owner-operator has the listed defects fixed at his or her own cost, at the company shop at a quoted rate or at an outside shop, and brings the tractor back for re-inspection.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the lease and pay schedule
steps.description: The coordinator fills in the standard lease template: pay per loaded and empty mile or a percentage of revenue, fuel surcharge passed through from the weekly table, the list of chargebacks with how each is computed, escrow amount, insurance responsibilities, notice period and start date. Non-standard terms are marked for approval.

error.defect_description: Chargeback or escrow terms written inconsistently with the settlement set-up.

control.basis: 49 CFR 376.12 written lease requirements (Truth-in-Leasing) for owner-operator equipment run in the US under the carrier's authority; applied fleet-wide by policy for Canadian trips

next.condition: non-standard rate, escrow or equipment terms

evidence.note: Lease contents (compensation, chargebacks with computation, escrow, insurance, duration) follow 49 CFR 376.12; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve non-standard terms
steps.description: The truckload operations manager reviews requests for a higher rate, a lower escrow, a dedicated lane or permission to haul for others, compares them with the rates paid to similar owner-operators, and approves, changes or refuses them.

control.basis: Company delegation of authority: operations manager approves non-standard owner-operator pay terms

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Owner-operator reviews and signs the lease
steps.description: The owner-operator reads the lease, often with an accountant, asks about deductions and fuel surcharge, and signs. Some applicants walk away at this point because another carrier offers more.

control.basis: 49 CFR 376.12 written lease requirements (Truth-in-Leasing) for owner-operator equipment run in the US under the carrier's authority; applied fleet-wide by policy for Canadian trips

evidence.note: Signature by both parties is required by 49 CFR 376.12(a); timing and walk-away share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Set up the owner-operator in settlements
steps.description: The settlements clerk creates the owner-operator as a vendor in the ERP and the TMS settlement module, enters the bank details from the void cheque, the pay rate, escrow, insurance and plate deductions, and links the fuel card. Bank details are entered by finance, not by the operations staff who signed the lease.

error.defect_description: A deduction amount or bank number is keyed wrong.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: vendor and bank master data maintained by finance, separate from the staff who negotiate terms

evidence.note: Separation of vendor bank set-up from operations is common internal control; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Apply for plates and add the unit to permits and insurance
steps.description: The coordinator adds the tractor to the carrier's apportioned (IRP) fleet and IFTA account, orders plates and a cab card, adds the unit to the carrier's safety fleet list and to the insurer's schedule, and orders US permits for cross-border units.

control.basis: International Registration Plan and International Fuel Tax Agreement registration for units running in more than one jurisdiction

evidence.note: Apportioned plates under the carrier's IRP account and IFTA decals are the usual arrangement for leased-on owner-operators in Canada; texts not opened, so tier C.

steps.name: Wait for plates and cab card
steps.description: The provincial registration office issues the apportioned plates and cab card, which are couriered to the terminal. Until they arrive the tractor cannot run loaded across jurisdictions under the carrier's account.

evidence.note: Plate issue times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Install the ELD and decals and issue the fuel card
steps.description: A technician installs and activates the company ELD and telematics unit, applies the carrier's name and safety numbers to the doors and mounts the plates; the coordinator hands over the fuel card. The tractor is now ready for dispatch.

evidence.note: ELDs required from June 2021 with progressive enforcement; installation times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Orient the owner-operator and hand over to a driver manager
steps.description: The driver manager who will dispatch the unit walks the owner-operator through the dispatch rules, trip paperwork, scanning of bills of lading, settlement timing and safety policies, and plans the first load.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the owner-operator's file at renewal or unit change
steps.description: Ahead of the lease anniversary or a tractor change, the coordinator reviews the owner-operator's insurance expiry, inspection date, safety record, settlement disputes and revenue, and asks the driver manager whether to renew.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the lease addendum
steps.description: The coordinator writes an addendum with the new rate, the replacement tractor's details or updated deductions, citing the clauses of the original lease that change.

control.basis: 49 CFR 376.12 written lease requirements (Truth-in-Leasing) for owner-operator equipment run in the US under the carrier's authority; applied fleet-wide by policy for Canadian trips

evidence.note: Changes to compensation and chargebacks must be in the written lease or an addendum (49 CFR 376.12(d), (h)); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Owner-operator signs the addendum
steps.description: The owner-operator reads the addendum, checks the new rate and deductions against recent settlements, sometimes negotiates the rate with the operations manager, and signs and returns it by email.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the settlement set-up
steps.description: The settlements clerk changes the pay rate, deductions or unit number in the TMS settlement module and the ERP vendor record so the next weekly settlement uses the new terms.

error.defect_description: New rate entered with the wrong effective date.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Process the termination notice
steps.description: The coordinator records who ended the lease and why, sets the last dispatch date in line with the notice period, and tells the driver manager, settlements, safety and the insurer.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Recover plates, fuel card, ELD and company equipment
steps.description: When the owner-operator returns to the terminal after the last trip, the coordinator collects the plates and cab card, cancels the fuel card, has the ELD removed and the company trailer returned, and removes the unit from the IRP fleet and insurance schedule.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Calculate the final settlement and escrow refund
steps.description: The settlements clerk waits for the last trip paperwork, fuel card transactions, tolls and repair invoices to arrive, deducts what is owed from the escrow, adds interest and pays the balance with an itemised statement.

control.basis: 49 CFR 376.12(k): final escrow accounting and return no later than 45 days after termination

evidence.note: Escrow accounting with interest and return within 45 days of termination under 49 CFR 376.12(k); holding period and dispute share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Rule on disputed final deductions
steps.description: The truckload operations manager reviews the disputed items, such as damage to a returned trailer or an unreturned plate, against the lease and the evidence, and decides what to refund.

evidence.note: Owner-operator contracting practice at Canadian truckload carriers 2019-2022 from general knowledge; times are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Declined applicant
exceptions.description: The applicant fails screening, driver qualification or the road test.

exceptions.name: Tractor fails intake inspection
exceptions.description: The owner-operator must repair defects and bring the tractor back.

exceptions.name: Missing or expired documents
exceptions.description: Insurance certificates or registration are missing and go back to the owner-operator.

exceptions.name: Applicant walks away at signing
exceptions.description: The applicant takes a better offer elsewhere after the lease is drafted.

exceptions.name: Disputed final settlement
exceptions.description: On termination the owner-operator disputes deductions from escrow and the operations manager rules.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from logging the action to its end state
benchmarks.population: Owner-operator contract actions at a Canadian truckload carrier (mix of applications, renewals and terminations)

evidence.note: Author's estimate: two to four weeks to lease on a new owner-operator, about a week for a renewal, and 30 to 45 days to close a termination because of the escrow holding period.

benchmarks.population: Owner-operator leases under US Truth-in-Leasing rules

pain_points.description: Onboarding waits on the applicant's documents, the driver trainer, the shop and the plate office in turn, so good applicants sign elsewhere.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge.

pain_points.description: Lease terms for chargebacks and escrow are typed again into the settlement system, and mismatches show up as disputes on the first settlements.

evidence.note: Chargebacks must be listed with their computation in the lease; the re-keying is the author's assumption.

pain_points.description: Final settlements are held for weeks waiting for late fuel and repair charges, and escrow deductions are a common source of disputes.

evidence.note: 45-day escrow rule; dispute frequency is the author's estimate.

sources.title: 49 CFR 376.12 - Written lease requirements
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (US Code of Federal Regulations)
sources.supports: Lease of owner-operator equipment to an authorized carrier: written lease signed by both parties stating start and end, exclusive possession and control by the carrier, compensation stated before any trip, chargeback items listed with how each is computed, payment within 15 days after submission of the delivery documents, a copy of the rated freight bill when pay is a percentage of revenue, written itemisation before cargo or damage deductions, escrow terms with interest and return within 45 days of termination.

sources.title: Enforcement of Canada's ELD mandate to be phased in over a year
sources.supports: Transport Canada kept the 12 June 2021 ELD mandate date with a 12-month progressive enforcement period of education and awareness; full enforcement expected from June 2022.

assumptions: Volume is set at 35 to 70 contract actions a month, above the organisation file's 6 to 16, because renewals, tractor changes and terminations are part of the process and new applications outnumber signed leases. The 6 to 16 figure fits signed new leases only.

US Truth-in-Leasing rules (49 CFR 376.12) bind leases for equipment run in the US under the carrier's authority; the carrier is assumed to use one lease form for all owner-operators, so the rules shape every lease.
Canadian National Safety Code standards, IRP and IFTA rules are described from general knowledge; their texts were not opened, so those steps are tier C.
Owner-operator time is shown for completeness and adds to the simulated hands-on hours, but it is not company labour: the role's fte_on_process is 0.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file. The owner-operator tractor resource has no running cost in the organisation file.
Cycle time mixes three paths: new leases about three weeks, renewals about a week, terminations about five weeks with the escrow holding period.
